tools.name: firebox_devices_list
tools.description: Retrieves a list of Fireboxes, FireClusters, and Access Points for the specified WatchGuard Cloud account. You can specify a type of device in the *device_type* parameter, to filter the list with Fireboxes and FireClusters (FB) or Access Points (AP) details. To get details of a specific device, specify the device ID in the *device* parameter. For Service Provider accounts, set *include_hierarchy* to true to include devices from Subscriber accounts. Subscriber accounts ignore this parameter. The *device* and *include_hierarchy* parameters are mutually exclusive. Optional: device_type, include_hierarchy (default: false), device. Returns array of FbxdeviceDetail.

params.description: Specifies the type of device to get in the response. Allowed values are `ALL` (Fireboxes, FireClusters, and Access Points), `FB` (Fireboxes and FireClusters only), `AP` (Access Points only). If not specified, all device types are returned. The *device* and *device_type* parameters are mutually exclusive.

Applicable only if the specified *accountid* is a Service Provider account. The *device* and *include_hierarchy* parameters are mutually exclusive. Allowed values are: true false. Default: false.

params.name: device
params.description: Specifies the device ID you want to get the details for. For, Access Points and FireClusters you must specify the `AP-` and `FBCL-` prefixes respectively. For example, `AP-12345`, `FBCL-266366`. For Fireboxes, the `FB-` prefix is optional. For example,`59432` or `FB-59432`. The *device* parameter cannot be combined with *include_hierarchy* or *device_type*.

novel_features.name: Cross-tenant endpoint posture
novel_features.description: List every endpoint that is unprotected, out of date, isolated, unlicensed or waiting on a reboot, across the accounts a Service Provider manages.

novel_features.name: Incident work queue
novel_features.description: See open ThreatSync incidents across your managed accounts, ranked by severity, threat score and age, with untouched incidents and recommended-but-not-taken actions called out.

novel_features.name: Cross-product tenant health
novel_features.description: One row per managed account: Fireboxes offline, endpoints at risk, open incidents by severity and licenses expiring soon (Service Provider accounts).

novel_features.name: Deployment wait
novel_features.description: Block until a Firebox deployment or certificate-install transaction finishes: exit 0 on complete, 8 on failed, 9 if still running at --max-wait.

novel_features.name: Fleet change diff
novel_features.description: After a sync, see which Fireboxes, FireClusters and Access Points went offline, came back, appeared, disappeared or changed firmware since the previous sync.

novel_features.name: Allocation reconcile
novel_features.description: Compare a Service Provider's Firebox allocations against the Fireboxes that actually report in, and summarize owned, allocated and available software licenses.

novel_features.name: Firmware lag
novel_features.description: From synced devices, find Fireboxes and Access Points running older firmware than the newest version seen for the same model in your fleet.

novel_features.name: CVE exposure pivot
novel_features.description: Group missing patches by CVE and criticality across managed accounts (needs WatchGuard Patch Management), showing which customers and devices are exposed.
